title: Boss: rebuild Test Case 9
brief:
Write `learn/test_tc09_search_product.py` from scratch, without looking at it. No starter code.

**The behaviour to prove:** searching the products page for *dress* returns dresses.

Everything a reviewer will look for:

- a test function named after the behaviour
- search for `dress` from the products page
- the **Searched Products** heading appears
- at least one product card is visible
- exactly **2** cards come back
- the names are read, printed, and checked for at least one containing "dress"

Every technique in this zone, in one function. When it passes, open `learn/test_tc09_search_product.py` and compare - you should recognise your own test.
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_search_for_a_dress(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    page.locator("#search_product").fill("dress")
    page.locator("#submit_search").click()

    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="Searched Products")).to_be_visible()

    results = page.locator(".productinfo")
    expect(results.first).to_be_visible()
    expect(results).to_have_count(2)

    names = page.locator(".productinfo p").all_inner_texts()
    print(f"Products found: {names}")
    dresses = [name for name in names if "dress" in name.lower()]
    assert len(dresses) > 0, "Expected at least one product with 'dress' in its name"

checks.label: The shop ran a search for "dress"
checks.feedback: No finished search for "dress". Fill #search_product, then click #submit_search.

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You assert both the heading and the first card are visible
checks.feedback: I counted fewer than two to_be_visible checks. Both matter, and they say different things: the heading proves the search ran, the card proves it returned something.

checks.name: to_have_count
checks.label: You assert exactly how many results there are
checks.feedback: No to_have_count check ran. "Some results" is a weak promise - say how many, and the test notices when the search starts over-matching.

checks.label: You read the product names
checks.feedback: No all_inner_texts() call reached the page. You need the actual names to check them.

checks.label: You print what you found
checks.feedback: Nothing was printed containing a product name. A print here is not debugging litter - when this test fails in CI at 3 a.m., the printed list is what tells you whether the search broke or the catalogue changed.

checks.label: Your test waited out the shop's response
checks.feedback: Your test finished too early for the results to have arrived, so the assertions were not looking at search results at all.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Six steps, in order: goto, fill, click, expect the heading, expect the cards (visible and count), then read and check the names.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Hold the cards in a variable: results = page.locator(".productinfo"). Then expect(results.first).to_be_visible() and expect(results).to_have_count(2) reuse the same address. .first is needed on the visibility check because eight - well, two - cards match, and strict mode will not pick for you.

reveal:
Assertion Ridge is cleared, and you have just reproduced one of the kit's 26 real tests.

The habit to carry forward: **an assertion is a promise about behaviour you have verified, waited for properly, and can defend in review.**

Ahead lie the Form Marshes, Cart Caverns, and eventually Page Object Peaks - where the question becomes how to keep tests this readable once there are two hundred of them. Those zones are mapped but not yet built; `site/CONTRIBUTING-CONTENT.md` explains how to add one, and it is a single JSON file.
